newsitem.title: TAIWAN: BA may buy China Airlines stake - paper.
newsitem.headline: BA may buy China Airlines stake - paper.

text.p: British Airways is likely to buy a 16 percent stake in Taiwan's China Airlines in a deal worth about T$6.3 billion, the local Economic Daily News reported on Tuesday.

The newspaper quoted unnamed sources as saying that after an initial evaluation, British Airways had shown keen interest in purchasing China Airlines shares to seek mutually beneficial ties with Taiwan's leading carrier.

In May, China Airlines said China Aviation Development Foundation -- the airline's major shareholder -- planned to release 210 million shares, or 16 percent of the firm's stake, in 1996 to diversify its shareholdings.

The move, which has been postponed to the first half of 1997 due to delays in approvals by the communications ministry, would reduce China Aviation Development Foundation's stake to 66 percent from 82 percent.
A spokeswoman for British Airways' Taiwan branch would not comment on the report. Calls to China Airlines were referred to the China Aviation Development Foundation.
At China Aviation, an executive overseeing the divestment said no deals had been set but that the plan would go forward in 1997, with foreign firms the only potential targets.
"The report surprised me," he said by telephone, asking that his name not be used. "We are still negotiating with interested foreign buyers and so far no deals have been made."
"We want foreign partners to forge strategic alliances to strengthen our competitiveness," he said.
"The ministry has in principle approved the plan and after receiving the formal approval document we'll soon complete the deal some time in the first half of 1997," he said.
The foundation has commissioned Hong Kong-based investment bank Wheelock Natwest to advise on the share release, he said.
